newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cabinet approves draft anti-dumping bill.
newsitem.headline: Czech cabinet approves draft anti-dumping bill.

text.p: The Czech cabinet approved a draft version of an anti-dumping law on Wednesday, but Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said he hoped it would not be used much.
Speaking at a news conference following a government meeting, Klaus said he saw the anti-dumping legislation as an "extreme, very marginal measure".
The measure puts the onus of anti-dumping complaints on industries who claim to be damaged by extraordinarily cheap imports. The bill must be approved by parliament.
Klaus said that each applicant who files a dumping complaint will have to post a one million crown deposit which will be returned if government agencies determine the complaint was justified.
Klaus said the measure would have a "standard" dumping definition.

A punitive tariff will be levied on the imported goods in violation of the law after the consideration of the parity of purchasing power in the Czech Republic and in the place of origin of the allegedly dumped product.
Further details of penalties under the new measure were not immediately available.
Klaus said the cabinet added a number of measures preventing companies from using it as a protectionist measure.
"It is a very extreme, very marginal law, ... it certainly can not have any measurable impact on macro (economic) figures," said Klaus.
